I was talking nonstop, jumping from one idea to another, starting three or four surveillance jobs at once, pacing my office because I couldn’t sit still. My thoughts felt like they were racing ahead of me, and I barely slept—maybe three hours a night—but didn’t feel tired. I go to work, I run the crane, I come home, but I feel hollow doing it. I’ve been avoiding the guys at the yard and even at home I mostly hide in the bedroom or in front of the TV. My wife keeps asking what’s wrong and I just shrug her off.

I get stuck on the smallest choices—what to eat, what to wear, even picking a show—I'll stand there frozen. At the same time I’m convinced I somehow cause bad things. Like if there’s an accident on the news, I’ll start thinking it happened because I didn’t double-check something at work or because of some stupid thing I said years ago.

Every now and then, especially when I’m up on the crane, I get these intense urges to just step off, or when a truck’s coming I picture myself walking in front of it. I don’t plan it, it just hits me.

Three weeks ago there was this stretch where my mood kept flipping—one minute I’d feel amped up, like I could take on anything, and the next I’d be snapping at everyone over nothing. I couldn’t sit still, pacing around the yard on breaks, fiddling with tools at home, starting little projects and then dropping them halfway through. I’d jump from fixing something in the garage to checking my phone to cleaning, without really finishing any of it. It didn’t exactly wreck my work, but it felt like I was always revving too high inside.
D009-D001_h018.question_a:

I come home from the yard and just sit in the living room, not talking to my wife or kids. I dodge calls from my buddies; even simple small talk feels like too much work.

I get stuck on the smallest choices—what to wear to work, what to make for dinner. I’ll stand in front of the fridge for ten minutes and still not decide. I’ve also been having these thoughts that every bad thing is somehow my fault—like when I hear about an accident on the news, I feel convinced I caused it by not paying attention at work or years ago doing something wrong. It doesn’t make sense, but it feels real. Sometimes, when I’m up on the crane or near traffic, I get these sudden urges to just step off or walk into the road. I haven’t planned anything, but the pull scares me.

About six months ago, before this stretch, I had about three weeks where I barely slept—maybe three hours a night and didn’t feel tired. My thoughts were flying, and I was talking a mile a minute, bouncing from one idea to the next. At work and at home I couldn’t sit still; I was pacing, starting projects all over the place—reorganizing the garage, online courses, extra shifts—never finishing any of it. My mood would flip on a dime: one moment I’d feel on top of the world, the next I’d snap at my wife over nothing. Outside those weeks, I’m not like that—I’m usually steady, not especially restless or scattered, and I sleep normally unless I’m in one of those “up” phases.
D009-D001_h018.question_b:
It’s hard to explain because I feel like there are two different things going on, but they kind of blur together.

Since I was a kid—like before middle school—people said I was “always on,” talking fast, bouncing from one thing to another, never able to sit still. That never really stopped. Even now, at 38, my mind races all the time, I get distracted mid‑sentence, start three projects at home and don’t finish any, and I sleep maybe 4–5 hours and still feel wired. That’s just my “normal,” according to my wife.

About three weeks ago, though, it ramped up. My mood’s been flipping fast—one minute I’m joking, the next I’m snapping at coworkers. On breaks I can’t just sit; I’m pacing, scrolling my phone, checking tools, like I can’t tolerate being idle. I jump between jobs around the house, leaving a mess of half‑done stuff.

But for the last four months overall, I’ve actually felt mostly…empty. Like there’s nothing there. I’ve been pulling back from friends, letting calls go, even with my kids I feel distant. I get stuck picking what to eat or what shirt to wear. I keep thinking stupid stuff like maybe that crane accident last year was somehow my fault, or even bad things on the news are because I’m a bad person. Sometimes when I’m up high at work, I get this sudden urge to just step off—not with a plan, just this impulse that scares me enough to back away.
